study type: Secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study
exposure: Maternal body mass index at delivery (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2 vs. < 30 kg/m2)
outcome: Unsuccessful operative vaginal delivery (defined as cesarean delivery after an attempted operative vaginal delivery)
cohort: Nulliparous women with cephalic live-born nonanomalous singleton pregnancies ≥ 34 weeks at delivery who had an attempted operative vaginal delivery (either forceps or vacuum)
finding: Nulliparous individuals with a BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2 at delivery were more likely to have an unsuccessful operative vaginal delivery attempt than those with a BMI < 30 kg/m2.
mod_finding: There was no evidence of interaction or effect modification by operative instrument type for the rate of unsuccessful operative vaginal delivery attempt, composite maternal morbidity, or composite neonatal morbidity.
